author: YillagerReviews
quote: This is by far my favorite release from Rockstar Games, the RPG elements of this game are incredible, you can make CJ skinny or fat, upgrade your swimming capabilities, upgrade your gun wielding efficiency, and your gang status. The humor is funny, and the story is incredible.

author: YillagerReviews
quote: This is one of my favorite releases by Sony Interactive Entertainment. This game evokes certain feelings throughout the game such as anger when Ryuzo betrays Jin, shock when Khotun Khan beheads Taka, sadness when your horse is mortally wounded at the beginning of act three, and in the end where you feel the loss of a father figure when you choose to kill or spare Lord Shimura.

author: YillagerReviews
quote: This is one of the most introspective titles released by Rockstar, and by far one of my favorites. The dark atmosphere of Liberty City, the backstory of Niko Bellic’s past, and ultimately the end makes this one of Dan Houser’s best works.

author: YillagerReviews
quote: This is genuinely one of the most disappointing releases from Rockstar. Grand Theft Auto V lacks the energy of its’ predecessors. It lacks the satirical humor of Grand Theft Auto V, it lacks the introspection and storytelling of Grand Theft Auto IV, it lacks the diverse RPG elements of San Andreas. I applaud it for having great graphics of course, but that was a trait inherited from Red Dead Redemption II. The reintroduction of Niko Bellic from Grand Theft Auto IV is interesting, but it feels “forced” as if it were a Marvel movie reintroducing Iron Man. The endings are “okay” at best. In the two endings, regardless of your actions, Lucia and Jason are both overwhelmed by police gunfire, but the third causes Jason to sacrifice everything, in turn for Lucia’s freedom and to meet up with his kid. Chores and housework aside, this is not the traditional Grand Theft Auto we have awaited for more than a decade.

author: YillagerReviews
quote: This game is genuinely one of the greatest games for the Nintendo Switch 2, and probably Nintendo’s catalogue. Few Nintendo games manage to reach an emotional effect, but the ending where Navi flies away genuinely creates a feeling of a friend you lost.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
